# awnest

> Prove there is a human before you let them into the nest.

Any surface an agent can use, a bot can flood. CAPTCHA is hostile to the humans it is meant to serve and is beaten by the machines it is meant to stop, so the check has to be something other than a puzzle -- and every check that does exist fails OPEN, because "we could not tell" and "it is fine" reach the caller as the same empty value.

## Install

```
pip install awnest
```

## Use it in 30 seconds

Gate one action behind a human check and watch an automated caller fail it.

## Composes with

- [awiam](https://aitherium.github.io/awiam/) — Who is this caller? A directory and session store that fails honestly.
- [awbac](https://aitherium.github.io/awbac/) — Role-based access control that fails closed and explains itself.
- [awdit](https://aitherium.github.io/awdit/) — An append-only audit trail whose gaps are DETECTABLE.
- [awseal](https://aitherium.github.io/awseal/) — Sign an artifact so a stranger can verify it.
- [awrelay](https://aitherium.github.io/awrelay/) — Portable agent messaging — findings, alerts, coordination.
- [awgit](https://aitherium.github.io/awgit/) — Semantic version control on top of git — edit-ops and leases.
- [awnet](https://aitherium.github.io/awnet/) — The agentic web — agents host a mesh, and agents join one.
- [awtunnel](https://aitherium.github.io/awtunnel/) — Reach a service that has no public address.
- [awdk](https://aitherium.github.io/awdk/) — Build AI agent fleets — 3 lines, any backend, local or cloud.
